newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No damaging cold in sight for Brazil coffee--Somar.
newsitem.headline: No damaging cold in sight for Brazil coffee--Somar.

text.p: No damaging cold is in sight for Brazilian coffee regions, with air masses in the region passing to the south of coffee growing areas, local meteorologist Somar said Tuesday.

An approaching polar air mass will pass quickly through the south of Parana this evening before moving out to the ocean, with minimum temperatures in the north of Parana and other coffee areas ranging between eight and 14 degrees Celsius, said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
Another cold front is expected to arrive in Brazil on Aug 7 but the associated air mass will only reach as far north as the southern state of Santa Catarina, he added.
In the more long-term outlook, the next air mass is only expected to reach the coffee areas on Aug 15, he added.

However, the air mass, currently in the Pacific, is very weak with an intensity of 1,020 millibars and long-term models also indicate the coffee regions will see cloudy weather during this period which should further remove the risk of damaging cold.
